title.en: LangChain Agents: Tools & the ReAct Pattern

description.en: Build AI agents that can use tools, make decisions, and follow the ReAct (Reason + Act) pattern to solve complex tasks.
description.ta: கருவிகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி, முடிவுகளை எடுத்து, சிக்கலான பணிகளைத் தீர்க்க ReAct வடிவத்தைப் பின்பற்றும் AI agents-ஐ உருவாக்குங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Robot Butler

Vaathiyaar introduces a robot. "Students, a chain follows a fixed path. But an AGENT decides its own path. Give it tools — a calculator, a web searcher, a database — and it decides which tool to use, when, and how many times. This is the ReAct pattern: Reason about what to do, then Act."

### Chain vs Agent

| Feature | Chain | Agent |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Path | Fixed, predetermined | Dynamic, decided at runtime |
| Tools | Not used | Can call tools |
| Loops | No | Yes — can retry and iterate |
| Use case | Simple pipelines | Complex, multi-step tasks |

### The ReAct Pattern

1. **Thought** — "I need to find the current weather"
2. **Action** — Call the weather tool
3. **Observation** — "Temperature is 32°C"
4. **Thought** — "Now I can answer the user"
5. **Final Answer** — "It's 32°C and sunny"

> **Key Insight:** Agents are powerful but less predictable than chains. Use chains when you know the exact steps; use agents when the steps depend on the data.
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் Robot Butler

வாத்தியார் ஒரு robot-ஐ அறிமுகப்படுத்துகிறார். "மாணவர்களே, chain ஒரு நிலையான பாதையைப் பின்பற்றும். ஆனால் AGENT தனது சொந்த பாதையை தீர்மானிக்கும்."

instruction.en: Build an agent's tools and its ReAct loop. LangChain cannot run in this offline sandbox, so the starter code has a mini `@tool` decorator and `FakeReActLLM`, a scripted LLM that replies in the ReAct format. 1) Complete the tools: `word_count(text)` returns the number of words as a string, `reverse_text(text)` returns the text reversed. 2) `parse_action(llm_output)` returns (tool_name, tool_input) from the 'Action: ...' and 'Action Input: ...' lines. 3) `run_agent(question, llm, tools, max_steps=5)`: start the prompt with 'Question: <question>\n'; on each step call `llm.invoke(prompt)` and append its output plus a newline to the prompt; if the output contains 'Final Answer:', return the text after it (stripped); otherwise run the chosen tool and append 'Observation: <result>\n'. Return None if max_steps run out.
instruction.ta: ஒரு agent-இன் tools மற்றும் அதன் ReAct loop-ஐ உருவாக்குங்கள். இந்த offline sandbox-ல் LangChain இயங்காது, எனவே starter code-ல் ஒரு சிறிய `@tool` decorator-உம், ReAct வடிவில் பதிலளிக்கும் scripted LLM ஆன `FakeReActLLM`-உம் உள்ளன. 1) Tools-ஐ நிறைவு செய்யுங்கள்: `word_count(text)` சொற்களின் எண்ணிக்கையை string ஆகத் திருப்புகிறது, `reverse_text(text)` text-ஐத் தலைகீழாகத் திருப்புகிறது. 2) `parse_action(llm_output)` 'Action: ...' மற்றும் 'Action Input: ...' வரிகளிலிருந்து (tool_name, tool_input) திருப்புகிறது. 3) `run_agent(question, llm, tools, max_steps=5)`: prompt-ஐ 'Question: <question>\n' என்று தொடங்குங்கள்; ஒவ்வொரு step-லும் `llm.invoke(prompt)`-ஐ அழைத்து அதன் output-ஐயும் ஒரு newline-ஐயும் prompt-ல் சேருங்கள்; output-ல் 'Final Answer:' இருந்தால் அதற்குப் பின் உள்ள text-ஐ (strip செய்து) திருப்புங்கள்; இல்லையெனில் தேர்ந்தெடுத்த tool-ஐ இயக்கி 'Observation: <result>\n'-ஐச் சேருங்கள். max_steps முடிந்துவிட்டால் None திருப்புங்கள்.

en: word_count: return str(len(text.split())); reverse_text: return text[::-1]
parse_action: loop over llm_output.splitlines(); check 'Action Input:' before 'Action:' because both start with 'Action'
run_agent: for _ in range(max_steps): output = llm.invoke(prompt); prompt += output + '\n'
If 'Final Answer:' in output return output.split('Final Answer:', 1)[1].strip(); else prompt += f'Observation: {tools[name].invoke(tool_input)}\n'
ta: word_count: str(len(text.split())) திருப்புங்கள்; reverse_text: text[::-1] திருப்புங்கள்
parse_action: llm_output.splitlines() மீது loop செய்யுங்கள்; இரண்டும் 'Action' என்று தொடங்குவதால் 'Action:'-க்கு முன் 'Action Input:'-ஐச் சரிபாருங்கள்
run_agent: for _ in range(max_steps): output = llm.invoke(prompt); prompt += output + '\n'
output-ல் 'Final Answer:' இருந்தால் output.split('Final Answer:', 1)[1].strip() திருப்புங்கள்; இல்லையெனில் prompt += f'Observation: {tools[name].invoke(tool_input)}\n'

practice_challenges.test_code:
assert word_count.name == "word_count" and "count" in word_count.description.lower(), "keep the @tool decorator and the docstring - the agent reads them"
assert word_count.invoke("Hello world from PyMasters") == "4", "word_count must return the word count as a string: '4'"
assert word_count.invoke("one") == "1", "word_count('one') must be '1'"
assert reverse_text.invoke("Python") == "nohtyP", "reverse_text('Python') must be 'nohtyP'"
_pa = parse_action("Thought: hmm\nAction: reverse_text\nAction Input: abc def")
assert _pa is not None and tuple(_pa) == ("reverse_text", "abc def"), "parse_action must return (tool_name, tool_input), got " + repr(_pa)
_tools = {t.name: t for t in [word_count, reverse_text]}
assert run_agent("q", FakeReActLLM(), _tools) == "4 words; reversed: nohtyP", "run_agent must run both tools and return the Final Answer text"


class _LoopLLM:
    def invoke(self, prompt):
        return "Thought: again\nAction: word_count\nAction Input: a b"


assert run_agent("q", _LoopLLM(), _tools, max_steps=3) is None, "run_agent must stop after max_steps and return None"
print("All agent tests passed!")

under_the_hood.summary: A LangChain agent repeatedly gives the model the question, the tool descriptions and the steps so far; the model replies with either a tool call or a final answer, and the executor runs the tool and appends the observation.

steps.title: Tools are described in the prompt
steps.body: Each tool has a name, a description and an argument schema, created for example with the @tool decorator on a Python function. These descriptions are sent with every model call. The model chooses a tool only from what the description says, so a vague description leads to wrong choices.

steps.title: Reason, act, observe
steps.body: For 'Is it warmer in Chennai or Delhi right now?': Thought, I need Chennai's temperature; Action, get_weather('Chennai'); Observation, 33 C. Then the same for Delhi, 24 C. Then: Final Answer, Chennai is warmer by 9 degrees. Each observation is appended so the next thought can use it.

steps.title: The executor runs the loop
steps.body: In the classic AgentExecutor, each round parses the model's output into a tool call or a finish. For a tool call it looks up the function, runs it, and appends the result to the scratchpad of intermediate steps. max_iterations (15 by default) stops a looping agent. Newer LangChain code builds the same loop with LangGraph.

props.caption: Intermediate steps sent back to the model

steps.title: Parsing is a failure point
steps.body: With text-based ReAct, the model must write 'Action:' and 'Action Input:' exactly; if it does not, parsing fails. handle_parsing_errors=True sends the error back so the model can correct itself. Native tool calling, where the API returns structured tool calls, avoids most of these errors.

steps.title: Chains versus agents
steps.body: A chain runs fixed steps in a fixed order, so it is predictable and cheap. An agent decides its steps at runtime, which handles open-ended tasks but costs more calls and can wander. Use a chain when you know the steps; reach for an agent when you do not.

under_the_hood.takeaway: A ReAct agent is a loop of model decisions and tool results. Good tool descriptions, a step limit and structured tool calls make it reliable; when the steps are known in advance, a plain chain is better.
